title: Father, I Bless Thy Gentle Hand
description: Father, I Bless Thy Gentle Hand in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 18, headed “Sanctified afflictions; or, Delight in the word of God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, I bless thy gen-tle hand; How kind was thy cha-stis-ing rod, That forc'd my con-science to a stand, And brought my wan-dering soul to God!

lines: Father, I bless thy gentle hand;
How kind was thy chastising rod,
That forc'd my conscience to a stand,
And brought my wandering soul to God!
Foolish and vain I went astray
Ere I had felt thy scourges, Lord,
I left my guide, and lost my way;
But now I love and keep thy word.
'Tis good for me to wear the yoke,
For pride is apt to rise and swell;
'Tis good to bear my Father's stroke,
That I might learn his statutes well.
The law that issues from thy mouth
Shall raise my cheerful passions more
Than all the treasures of the south,
Or western hills of golden ore.
Thy hands have made my mortal frame,
Thy spirit form'd my soul within;
Teach me to know thy wondrous Name,
And guard me safe from death and sin.
Then all that love and fear the Lord
At my salvation shall rejoice;
For I have hoped in thy word,
And made thy grace my only choice.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
